Definition: from G1537 and G2865; to bear forth (to burial):--carry out.
BiblicalUsage: This word means to carry out, to bear a body to burial, and it occurs once, at the gate of Nain. As Jesus comes near the gate, a dead man is carried out, the only son of a widow, and a great crowd follows her, and Jesus touches the bier and says, Young man, I say unto thee, arise. The carrying out becomes a carrying home.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Jesus meets us at the gate of our grief, because He stopped a funeral and gave a son back to his mother.
